confidence: high — verified directly against current Anthropic documentation and the Claude API reference
guidance: Use XML-style section tags (e.g. <context>, <instructions>, <example>) once a prompt has three or more distinct parts. Short, single-idea prompts don't need them.
When examples are used, keep to 3-5, each wrapped consistently (e.g. in <example> tags).
For long reference material, place the material before the instructions/question, not after — this ordering is documented to improve response quality.
A short, direct one-line role statement is enough when a role is genuinely warranted. An elaborate persona backstory adds no measurable value.
For agentic or multi-step tasks, distinguish clearly between what the model should just DO versus what it should only SUGGEST or ask about first.
avoid: Adding 'think step by step', 'take your time', or similar reasoning-scaffolding instructions — current Claude models reason adaptively by default, so this is redundant token spend, not a quality lever.
Adding an explicit self-verification / 'double-check your work' instruction — current Claude models already do this unprompted; adding it is redundant.
Aggressive 'CRITICAL: you MUST' style tool-triggering language — documented to cause over-triggering.
